questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: Entropy from enthalpy and free energy
questions.learningObjective: Compute ΔS from ΔG and ΔH
questions.stem: ΔH = 90 kJ/mol, ΔG = 60 kJ/mol at 300 K. Find ΔS in J/mol·K.
questions.explanation: ΔS = (ΔH - ΔG)/T = (90-60)/300 = 0.10 kJ/mol·K = 100 J/mol·K. Using ΔG-ΔH gives -100, which is wrong.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: Bond enthalpies for a diatomic reaction
questions.learningObjective: Explain bond enthalpy calculation
questions.stem: Explain how to estimate ΔH using bond enthalpies.

answer.exemplar: Sum the bond enthalpies of all bonds broken in reactants, subtract the sum of bond enthalpies of all bonds formed in products. Broken bonds are positive, formed bonds are negative, giving net ΔH.

questions.explanation: ΔH ≈ Σ(bonds broken) - Σ(bonds formed). Broken bonds cost energy, formed bonds release energy.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: Bond enthalpies for a combustion
questions.learningObjective: Compute ΔH of combustion
questions.stem: For C2H4 + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 2H2O, bond enthalpies C=C 614, C-H 413, O=O 498, C=O 799, O-H 463. Find ΔH in kJ.
questions.explanation: Bonds broken = 614 + 4*413 + 3*498 = 3760; bonds formed = 4*799 + 4*463 = 5048; ΔH = -1288 kJ. Forgetting a bond gives a less negative value.
questions.hint: Count all bonds in reactants and products.
